TestRuntimeSSHConfigWithRemediation (tests/e2e/serial/main_test.go) is the single most expensive test in the e2e-aws-serial suite: mean ~33 min, i.e. ~34% of the whole serial suite (~97 min), and its runtime is suspiciously stable (32m41s-32m56s across 9 recent master runs).

Root cause (confirmed from build logs, e.g. PR #1124 build 2074431700057722880):
The test binds a single-rule scan (sshd_disable_gssapi_auth, profile e8, from the runtime_sshd broken-content image) with AutoApplyRemediations=true, then calls f.WaitForRemediationToBeAutoApplied(). No ComplianceRemediation object is ever created for that rule, so the wait polls the full Timeout (30m, tests/e2e/framework/constants.go:7) and times out. The error is swallowed by t.Logf (main_test.go:2491, non-fatal), the re-scan comes back Compliant via the runtime config, the SSH check PASSes, and the test PASSes.

Impact:
- ~30 min wasted every serial run for a remediation code path that is never exercised.
- The test provides zero MachineConfig-remediation coverage despite its name; it effectively only validates the runtime SSH check.

Note: the e2e MachineConfigPool wiring is correct - the scan targets node-role.kubernetes.io/e2e and the MC role resolves to 'e2e' (GetFirstNodeRole), so the pool is NOT the problem.

Proposed fix (to be finalized): either (a) bound/guard the remediation wait so the test does not burn 30m when no remediation is produced, or (b) make the test actually generate and apply a MachineConfig remediation and assert on it (fail fast if absent). Decision on intent pending.
items.toString:
TestRuntimeSSHConfigWithRemediation (tests/e2e/serial/main_test.go) is the single most expensive test in the e2e-aws-serial suite: mean ~33 min, ~34% of the whole serial suite (~97 min), almost all of it a 30-minute dead wait.

*Root cause (corrected)*

The sshd_disable_gssapi_auth fix in the runtime_sshd content ships TWO MachineConfig variants gated by OCP version via the complianceascode.io/ocp-version annotation: one for <4.13.0 and one for >=4.13.0. The operator aggregator (shouldSkipRemediation) skips the variant that does not match the cluster, so on a modern cluster only the >=4.13.0 variant is generated. Because the fix yields two objects, the generated ComplianceRemediation name carries an index suffix: <scan>-sshd-disable-gssapi-auth-1. The <4.13.0 variant (the base name, no suffix) is never created.

The test hard-coded the base name and called WaitForRemediationToBeAutoApplied on it, so it waited for a remediation that never exists on 4.13+ clusters, polled the full 30m Timeout (tests/e2e/framework/constants.go), timed out (logged non-fatally at main_test.go:2491), and passed anyway on the runtime check - without ever waiting for the remediation it actually applied.

Confirmed from the run gather (PR #1124, build 2074431700057722880): the only SSH MachineConfig present is 75-test-runtime-ssh-remediation-scan-sshd-disable-gssapi-auth-1, labeled machineconfiguration.openshift.io/role: e2e. So the e2e MachineConfigPool wiring is correct - only the hard-coded wait-target name was wrong.

*Fix (PR #1303)*

Discover the scan's remediations by the compliance.openshift.io/scan-name label instead of hard-coding a name, wait for whatever was actually generated to roll out, and unapply the same set on cleanup. Removes the ~30m timeout and makes the test genuinely exercise the remediation apply/rollout path it claims to. Version-agnostic.

PR: https://github.com/ComplianceAsCode/compliance-operator/pull/1303

Tests using custom content images (e.g., from compliance-operator content PRs) fail intermittently when the compliance-operator pod restarts during test execution.

 **Problem:** When the compliance-operator restarts (node reboot, pod crash, rolling update), ProfileBundles that were created with custom content images get reverted back to default images. This causes test failures because the custom content (rules, profiles, remediations) is no longer available.

**Observable behavior:**

1. Test starts with custom content image (e.g., `quay.io/wsato/ocp4-content:latest`) 
2. ProfileBundles (`ocp4`, `rhcos4`) created successfully with custom image 
3. Operator pod restarts (for any reason) 
4. ProfileBundles now have default image (`ghcr.io/complianceascode/k8scontent:latest`) 
5. Test fails because expected custom rules/profiles are missing 

**Impact:** 

- Tests are unreliable when operator restarts occur 

- PR testing for content changes becomes flaky 

- Manual test reruns required, slowing down development 

**Environment:** 

- ocp4e2e test suite 

- Any test using custom content images (e.g., content PR builds)

*Rule type / scope:* test infrastructure (e2e).

We need an e2e suite that can validate the OpenShift Virtualization (CIS VM Extension) profiles end-to-end, so the OCP-Virt rule content (this epic) is continuously verified against a real cluster.

*Current state (ComplianceAsCode/ocp4e2e, default branch {{main}}):*
* The harness is parameterized by {{-profile}}, {{-product}} (ocp4/rhcos4), {{-content-image}}, {{-test-type}} (platform/node/all); entrypoints {{TestPlatformCompliance}}, {{TestNodeCompliance}}, {{TestProfile}}, {{TestProfileRemediations}}.
* ProfileBundle setup ({{helpers/utilities.go}} ensureTestProfileBundles) sets {{ContentFile: ssg-<product>-ds.xml}} only - i.e. the XCCDF/SCAP datastream. It does NOT set {{celContentFile}}.
* Setup installs only the Compliance Operator; it has no notion of installing OpenShift Virtualization.

*Gaps to close:*
# Install the OpenShift Virtualization (CNV) operator as a test setup step: create the {{openshift-cnv}} namespace, an OperatorGroup, and a Subscription for the {{kubevirt-hyperconverged}} operator; create the {{HyperConverged}} CR and wait until it is Available before scanning. The suite should be self-contained (install CNV if absent), gated by a flag/env (e.g. {{-install-virt}}) and idempotent if CNV is already present. Tear down / leave-in-place per existing setup conventions.
# CEL ProfileBundle support: the cis-vm-extension profile is {{scanner_type: CEL}}, delivered via the ProfileBundle {{celContentFile}} field - not the XCCDF datastream. Extend the harness ProfileBundle setup to populate {{celContentFile}} so CEL profiles parse and scan.
# Scanner RBAC: apply the extended RBAC from CMP-4425 so CEL rules can read kubevirt.io / cdi.kubevirt.io / k8s.cni.cncf.io / sriovnetwork.openshift.io resources. Without it, CEL fetches degrade to empty and results are misleading.
# Assertion generation for the CEL + mixed rule set: the OCP-Virt profile mixes CEL platform rules with manual (who-can) and OpenSCAP node rules. Generate/assert expected per-rule results appropriately (manual rules -> MANUAL, node rules via node scan or skipped).
# A Make target / CI lane to run the cis-vm-extension profile (platform) on the cluster (which the suite has provisioned with CNV).

*Acceptance criteria:*
* The suite installs the OpenShift Virtualization operator (and HyperConverged CR) during setup on a cluster that does not already have it, and no-ops if it is present.
* ocp4e2e can install a CEL ProfileBundle (celContentFile) and run the cis-vm-extension profile end-to-end.
* Per-rule expected results are asserted for the implemented CEL rules (the 5 fixed + newly added).
* A CI lane (or a documented manual run) executes the full flow: install CNV -> apply CMP-4425 RBAC -> scan cis-vm-extension -> assert results.
* Suite is green against the current cis-vm-extension profile.

*Related:* depends on CMP-4425 (scanner RBAC) for VM/network rule coverage; relates to CMP-3202 (CI job to test CO profiles on OCPVirt).

  PROFILE=cis-vm-extension PRODUCT=ocp4 \
  INSTALL_OPERATOR=<true|false> INSTALL_VIRT=true \

items.toString:
We have a series of tests we run on patches. Some are integration tests, some are unit tests, and other are for Konflux builds.

As a contributor, it’s nice to have a quick snapshot of what’s failing across various jobs, and the overall pass rate. Then, I can use that information to dig into specific issues to make things better.

Most of the recent Prow CI job information is publicly available from [https://prow.ci.openshift.org/prowjobs.js|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/prowjobs.js] - which we can query unauthenticated to get job results. We can write a script to filter these results down into the ones that are only applicable to the Compliance Operator repository, then add additional LLM-based analysis on top. The key part is that we’re deterministic in finding the data we want (instead of pointing Claude to [https://prow.ci.openshift.org/prowjobs.js|https://prow.ci.openshift.org/prowjobs.js] directly and having it burn tokens figuring it out each time).

A /ci-activity skill could be really useful and improve the developer experience by giving contributors a way to check CI daily and track job pass rates over time.

As a contributor, I want integration tests to run nightly instead of on every PR so that I get faster CI feedback and we reduce AWS costs.


Once unit test coverage is sufficient (tracked as a separate story in the parent epic), reconfigure CI to run e2e test suites as periodic nightly jobs rather than on every pull request. Keep a minimal smoke-test suite (e.g., perhaps the config or deployment) on PRs if needed. Update CI configuration and documentation to reflect the new workflow.

Acceptance Criteria:

* E2e test suites run as nightly periodic jobs (not triggered per-PR)
* PR CI completes in minutes (unit tests + lint + build), not hours
* Nightly results are visible to the team (notifications on failure - which can be done through [openshift/release Prow configuration|https://docs.ci.openshift.org/how-tos/notification/])
* A process exists to promote a nightly failure back to the PR that caused it
* AWS CI costs decrease measurably in the month following the change
* Contributors can still trigger a full e2e run manually on a PR when needed (e.g., /test e2e comment)

As a contributor, I want to know what code our integration tests actually cover so that we can identify the coverage gap between e2e and unit tests.


Go 1.20+ supports {{go build -cover}} to produce instrumented binaries that emit coverage data at runtime. Apply this to the compliance-operator binary used in e2e test runs so that integration test suites produce coverage profiles. We can do this in the [openshift/release CI steps|https://github.com/openshift/release/blob/main/ci-operator/config/ComplianceAsCode/compliance-operator/ComplianceAsCode-compliance-operator-master.yaml] - or in the project’s [makefile tooling|https://github.com/ComplianceAsCode/compliance-operator/blob/master/Dockerfile.ci#L10]. Aggregate these profiles into a report that can be compared against the unit test baseline.

Acceptance Criteria:

* After an e2e run completes, a coverage profile is produced and can be viewed with {{go tool covdata}}(tacked onto the e2e steps in the Makefile)
* Contributors can view coverage reports in e2e test artifacts
* The e2e coverage report excludes the same generated files as unit test coverage
* The {{-cover}} flag is never used in an image outside of CI testing (or bound of production)

items.toString: This work item links to "openshift/release#81024: CMP-4376: compliance-operator - skip e2e jobs for renovate.json changes (Web Link)"

items.fromString:
PRs to ComplianceAsCode/compliance-operator that only modify renovate.json (Renovate bot dependency configuration) are triggering all 7 e2e test suites (e2e-aws-parallel, e2e-aws-serial, e2e-aws-deployment, e2e-aws-scan-config, e2e-rosa, and ARM variants). These tests provision full AWS/ROSA clusters and are expensive in both time and cloud resources.

* PASS or NOT-APPLICABLE by default, or;
* PASS after remediation is applied, or;
* FAIL if no remediation exists.

Some notes and observations:

* There is no need to un-apply remediations in between scans
* Rules using variables may affect results for different profiles
** Remediating these rules may cause them to conflict with each other

items.fromString:
Bump the Compliance Operator Go toolchain to go1.25.11 (latest 1.25.x) and refresh dependencies to their latest patch releases. go1.25.11 carries the Go standard-library security fixes flagged against the compliance-operator-bundle image, clearing these (mostly overdue) CVE trackers:

* CVE-2026-33810 (CMP-4237) - crypto/x509 certificate validation bypass via incorrect DNS constraint application
* CVE-2026-32283 (CMP-4246) - crypto/tls DoS via multiple TLS 1.3 key-update messages
* CVE-2026-32280 (CMP-4243) - crypto/x509 DoS in certificate chain building
* CVE-2026-32281 (CMP-4290) - crypto/x509 DoS via inefficient certificate chain validation
* CVE-2026-32282 (CMP-4240) - os.Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root

All five are Go standard library issues, so the toolchain bump is the fix (no per-CVE code or base-image change). k8s.io/* dependencies stay within v0.35 (.3 -> .5) to preserve the pinned API surface; vendor/ is refreshed. go directive set to 1.25.11; build/Dockerfile uses the floating golang:1.25 tag and picks up the patched toolchain at build time.

Two PRs:
* master
* release-1.9 (backport for the 1.9.1 z-stream)

- 31 rules remain failing (14.8% of applicable rules)

Transition Compliance Operator CI jobs to the aws-stackrox cluster profile used by ACS.
